title: perf(canary): KV-aware hysteresis and sensitivity tuning for automated detection + rollout guards
author: Avery Chen
description: Context: Our performance canary system automatically detects latency/throughput regressions and gates rollouts. We observed noisy alerts and intermittent rollback flapping for workloads with heavy KV-cache behavior (long-tail sequence reuse), and sensitivity tuning was causing false positives when models moved between architectures. This PR adds a KV-aware hysteresis window, per-workload sensitivity profiles, and improved rollout guards to reduce noisy detections while preserving fast safety responses. Changes include new detection heuristics, metrics, CI+e2e test harness updates, and documentation. Motivation: reduce false-positive canary failures, avoid unnecessary rollback churn, and make tuned sensitivity profiles available for known KV-heavy workloads. Scope: runtime detector, canary controller, canary UI thresholds, and test harness. Testing: unit tests for detector math, load tests simulating KV-heavy prefix reuse, and integration tests validating rollout guard state transitions. Related: ENG-2148, ENG-2209, incident SUP-9821.
